scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: MAJOR REVERSAL PATTERNS: HEAD AND SHOULDERS TOP & BOTTOM

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. The Three Peak Anatomy. A Head and Shoulders top features a prominent central peak (head) flanked by two lower, roughly symmetrical crests (left and right shoulders).
beats.en_subtitle: Pillar one: 1. The Three Peak Anatomy. A Head and Shoulders top features a prominent central peak (head) flanked by two lower, roughly symmetrical crests (left and right shoulders).
beats.en_narration: Pillar one: 1. The Three Peak Anatomy. A Head and Shoulders top features a prominent central peak (head) flanked by two lower, roughly symmetrical crests (left and right shoulders).

cards.title: 1. The Three Peak Anatomy
cards.desc: A Head and Shoulders top features a prominent central peak (head) flanked by two lower, roughly symmetrical crests (left and right shoulders).

cards.title: 2. The Volume Confirmation Pattern
cards.desc: Volume is heaviest on the left shoulder, noticeably lighter on the head, contracts sharply on the right shoulder, and explodes on the neckline breakdown.

cards.title: 3. The Neckline Trigger
cards.desc: The neckline connects the intervening reaction lows; the reversal pattern is formally completed only when prices close decisively below this neckline support.

cards.title: 4. The Minimum Price Objective
cards.desc: Calculated by measuring the vertical distance from the head peak down to the neckline, and projecting that exact distance downward from the breakout point.

beats.hindi_tts: First: 1. A prior trend must exist for a reversal pattern to take place: you cannot reverse what is not there..

steps: 1. A prior trend must exist for a reversal pattern to take place: you cannot reverse what is not there.
2. The first warning of a Head & Shoulders top is when the head makes a new high on noticeably lighter volume.
3. The right shoulder must fail to exceed the head peak, signaling exhausted buyer demand.
4. The formation is complete only upon a decisive closing violation beneath the neckline support.
5. A return move (pullback) back up to test the broken neckline is common, but volume must remain light.
6. The minimum measuring price target is the vertical distance from the head to neckline projected from breakout.
7. Inverse Head & Shoulders bottoms require a significant surge in trading volume on the neckline breakout.
8. If the right shoulder rallies above the head peak, the entire reversal pattern is immediately invalidated.
